reason: The tetragonal metric (a about 7.068 A, c about 5.292 A) and likely Z=1 are well supported by peak positions, but the submitted P4/mmm atomistic model is not sufficiently established for exact recovery. No comparable whole-pattern Rwp was supplied, and the trajectory optimized a custom selected-peak intensity objective rather than performing a full-profile refinement against competing structures. It left genuine peaks near 28.25 and 38.19 degrees substantially underpredicted and displaced from the model's weak 210/300 reflections, while the model also predicts weak reflections such as 100 near 12.51 degrees that are not observed. The unconstrained coordinate result was Pm/Pmm2 at ordinary tolerances and became P4/mmm only at a loose 0.2 A tolerance before coordinates were manually snapped to rational special positions. Physical validation was limited to nearest-distance reporting: the submitted realization places every atom at z=0 or 1/2, leaves one Nb coordinated only by Nb within 3 A, gives Ag only two S neighbors, and creates many 2.499 A S-S contacts, so its chemistry is not persuasive. Element-order enumeration was confined to this imposed orbit model and even produced a distinct close-scoring Nb/S ordering, without a rigorous full-profile or chemical comparison. A materially different lower-symmetry/coordinate model could plausibly improve both fit and plausibility, so another solution attempt is warranted.
